newsitem.title: USA: Computer hardware firms seen with mixed Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Computer hardware firms seen with mixed Q2 results.

text.p: Computer hardware companies are expected to report mixed results in the second quarter, with only a few candidates for upside surprises, as some sluggishness persists in certain pockets of the industry.
Currency will also be a negative, but its impact will be less compared with first quarter for firms with Japanese operations, as the yen strengthened against the dollar.
Better-than-expected earnings from Compaq Computer Corp last week has fueled a rally in PC and PC-related stocks and Sequent Computer Systems had bullish news.
But for the most part, analysts said they expect major U.S. computer hardware makers to meet Wall Street estimates.
"I think the numbers, for most of the companies, will be in line," said Jay Stevens, an analyst at Buckingham Research. "You would think the market knows something, the way the stocks are going up."
Later this week, Sun Microsystems Inc is expected to be among the highlights of the computer hardware group, as strong server sales may help its earnings exceed estimates.
Sequent Computer will also report this week, after the company announced a record order from Boeing Co that fueled a jump in its stock on Monday.

Big systems makers, such as International Business Machines Corp, are expected to report on target earnings. IBM's second quarter will be similar to its first quarter, analysts said, with strength in PCs, disk drives and services offsetting sluggishness in AS/400 minicomputers. Its RS/6000 workstations and mainframes are expected to decline.
"I think they will come very close to consensus numbers," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst. The First Call consensus estimate for IBM is $1.42 a share.
Mainframes should improve, due to its new models unveiled earlier this quarter, but they are an increasingly smaller portion of overall revenues for the computer giant.

Another upside surprise could come from Digital Equipment Corp. John Jones of Salomon Brothers said he expects Digital to meet or beat his estimate of $0.73 a share, including a negative impact of currency of $0.40-$0.50/share.
Digital's PC business is now growing again, analysts said but its Alpha server business is probably flat or down.

In the PC sector, PC leader Compaq set a strong precedent, but Intel Corp's earnings later Tuesday will be closely watched for any indicators of the rest of the year. Intel spooked the technology sector at the end of May when it said its second quarter would not meet forecasts, but both Compaq and Dell have said they see no sluggishness in PCs.
At the other end of the PC arena, troubled Apple Computer Inc could lose more money than previously expected.

"However...the exact magnitude of the company's operating loss or the sharpness of its revenue decline is not nearly as important as the trends seen in its operational results," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Research analyst. Apple last week forced out Gil Amelio, its second CEO outster in 17 months.

Gateway 2000 Inc late last month forecast that its results will be below Wall Street estimates, a shortfall analysts attributed to some sluggishness earlier in the quarter in the consumer sector of the PC business.
Analysts said that new technologies coming out in the secod half of this year, including higher-end PCs with DVD players, should stimulate more demand in the consumer market.
